::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Purpose and companion files.** This brief is prepared for the consultancy economics team and Dr John Nellthorp (ITS, University of Leeds). It sets out a concise, first-principles active travel uptake method aligned with *Active Mode Benefits: Theoretical Framework* [@nellthorp2026], illustrates it on the **`r s$tot_len_km` km Oxfordshire-to-Uxbridge** section, and highlights eight modelling decisions to agree before scaling to the full {{< var corridor_total_km >}} km North–South Greenway. Prototype audits, full PCT/Bass equations, AMAT validation, supplementary diagnostics, and the 4-table data contract sit in [Methods & Appendix](methods.qmd).
:::

## Executive Summary & Decisions to Agree {#sec-decisions}

- **Corridor exposure matters:** Attenuating *Go Dutch* by alignment and access distance ($\omega_{ij}$) with $\kappa = 0.50$ reduces 3 km catchment uptake from +`r comma(round(s$du_new_3km))` (unattenuated ceiling) to **+`r comma(round(s$cc_new_3km))` new commute cyclists** (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", s$cc_share_3km)` mode share), of whom **+`r comma(round(s$cc_new_core))` (`r sprintf("%.0f%%", s$core_share_of_new)`)** sit on tightly aligned core OD pairs.
- **E-bikes unlock rural inter-town links:** Conventional cycling peaks at `2–6 km`, whereas e-bikes unlock `6–15 km` market-town corridors (`King's Sutton–Banbury`, `Wendover–Aylesbury`, `Chalfont St Peter–Uxbridge`).
- **Leisure & ramp-up shift the BCR materially:** Commuting is only {{< var nts_cycle_commute_pct >}} of cycling trips nationally; omitting leisure understates rural greenway demand 3–5×, while a realistic 5-year behavioural ramp-up reduces 40-year commute PVB by **`r sprintf("%.1f%%", s$amat_lag_drop_pct)`** (from £`r sprintf("%.1f", s$amat_tot_inst)`m to **£`r sprintf("%.1f", s$amat_tot_lag)`m** on the core commute subset).
- **Clear separation for appraisal:** Route diversion, car/PT mode shift, and newly generated *Exercise & Pleasure* trips ($VTT = 0$) are kept strictly separate to comply with @nellthorp2026 double-counting rules.

```{r tbl-decisions}
#| tbl-colwidths: [5, 22, 40, 33]
tbl_from_csv(
  "data/uptake_decisions.csv",
  caption = "Eight methodological choices to confirm before scaling to the 805.6 km North–South Greenway.",
  align = c("r", "l", "l", "l"),
  col_names = c("#", "Decision Area", "Options to Consider", "Recommended Default & Rationale")
)
```

## First-Principles Uptake Method {#sec-method}

Following @nellthorp2026 (§3.1.1), demand modelling and welfare valuation must be specified jointly using the same Generalised Cost ($GC_r = -U_r / \beta$; @wardman2020) attributes on route $r$ connecting $(i, j)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
GC_{ij,r} &= \sum_{n \in r} \Bigl( m\,v_t\,t_n + v_s\,s_n + v_e\,e_n + v_c\,c_n \Bigr) + \frac{U_{\text{pre}} + U_{\text{post}}}{\beta} \\
          &\approx \int_{0}^{T_r} \Bigl[ \beta + q(t) + e(t) \Bigr]\,\mathrm{d}t + \frac{U_{\text{pre}} + U_{\text{post}}}{\beta}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-gc}

where $t_n$ is travel time (access multiplier $m = 2.0$), $s_n$ is **perceived safety threat** (the dominant cycling deterrent; @dft2024ntas), $e_n$ is **net physical exertion** (MET-hours, lower for e-bikes), $c_n$ is **ambience and comfort** (upgrading to an off-road segregated track is valued at **{{< var ambience_offroad_rate >}}** in 2023 prices; @dft2025amat), and $q(t)$ captures continuous traffic/surface conditions [@kouwenhoven2023].

That cost reduction $\Delta GC_{ij} < 0$ drives three margins that appraisal must keep separate:

1. **Route choice (diversion):** Existing cyclists switch from parallel A/B roads onto the greenway ($\text{new trips} = 0$; Journey Ambience & external safety benefits only).
2. **Mode choice (mode shift):** Existing travellers switch from car, PT, or walking onto cycling (Rule-of-a-Half $\Delta CS$, full TATE3030/AMAT health & absenteeism benefits, plus TAG Unit A5.4 car-diversion MECs).
3. **Trip generation (induced demand):** New utility or *Exercise & Pleasure* trips (Rule-of-a-Half $\Delta CS$ with $VTT = 0$ for Exercise & Pleasure, full health benefits, zero car decongestion MECs).

To avoid crediting 100% of an area-wide *Go Dutch* network scenario [@lovelace2017] to a single linear greenway, we attenuate each 2011 Census OD pair by a dimensionless **corridor exposure weight** $\omega_{ij} \in [0, 1]$:

$$
\omega_{ij} = \phi_{ij} \cdot \exp\!\left(-\frac{a_i + a_j}{L_a}\right)
$$ {#eq-omega}

where $\phi_{ij} \in [0, 1]$ is the desire-line share within a 1.5 km corridor buffer, $a_i, a_j$ are endpoint centroid distances (m) to the spine, and $L_a = 3{,}000\text{ m}$. Steady-state commute cyclists $C^{1}_{ij}$ are then bounded between observed baseline $C^{0}_{ij}$ and the PCT upper-envelope reference $C^{\text{ref}}_{ij}$ (*Go Dutch* Central $\kappa = 0.50$; *E-bikes* High $\kappa = 0.60$):

$$
C^{1}_{ij} = \min\!\Bigl(N_{ij},\; C^{0}_{ij} + \kappa\,\omega_{ij}\,\max\bigl(0,\; C^{\text{ref}}_{ij} - C^{0}_{ij}\bigr)\Bigr)
$$ {#eq-corridor-uptake}

Full PCT logistic equations and an audit of the existing `railactive` prototype scripts are given in [Methods & Appendix](methods.qmd#sec-pct-details) (see also the [prototype audit](methods.qmd#sec-audit)).

## Oxfordshire–Uxbridge Case Study (`r s$tot_len_km` km) {#sec-casestudy}

We test the framework on the **`r s$tot_len_km` km Oxfordshire-to-Uxbridge** spine ({{< var corridor_version >}}, Sections `13` to `11`, `r s$n_links` links from Banbury via Brackley, Calvert, Aylesbury, Wendover, and Amersham to Uxbridge). Over **`r sprintf("%.0f%%", s$offroad_pct)` (`r s$offroad_km` km)** consists of off-road or segregated assets (detailed breakdown in [Methods & Appendix](methods.qmd#sec-more-examples)).

```{r fig-corridor-map}
#| fig-cap: "Oxfordshire–Uxbridge corridor case study: (A) Preferred alignment by infrastructure class and 3 km buffer; (B) 2011 Census LSOA commute uptake desire lines (Corridor Central >= 2.5 new cyclists; King's Sutton to Banbury highlighted)."
#| fig-width: 10.5
#| fig-height: 5.2
#| dpi: 300
plot_corridor_map(dat)
```

Across all inter-LSOA 2011 Census commute pairs ($\le 20\text{ km}$) within 3 km of the spine (**`r comma(s$n_pairs_3km)` OD pairs**, **`r comma(s$tot_comm_3km)` commuters**; `r sprintf("%.1f%%", s$car_pct_3km)` car driver, `r sprintf("%.1f%%", s$walk_pct_3km)` walking, **`r sprintf("%.2f%%", s$base_cyc_pct_3km)` cycling**), the **core corridor-aligned subset** (endpoints $\le 1.5\text{ km}$, $\phi_{ij} \ge 0.70$, distance $1.5\text{–}20\text{ km}$) isolates **`r comma(s$n_pairs_core)` pairs** and **`r comma(s$tot_comm_core)` commuters** (`r sprintf("%.2f%%", s$base_cyc_pct_core)` baseline cycling).

```{r tbl-scenarios}
tbl_scenarios(dat)
```

Three appraisal lessons emerge directly from @tbl-scenarios and @fig-dist-lad:

1. **Exposure attenuation prevents over-claiming:** Unattenuated *Go Dutch* (+`r comma(round(s$du_new_3km))`) overstates single-corridor impact; attenuating by $\omega_{ij}$ yields **+`r comma(round(s$cc_new_3km))`** Central new cyclists (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", s$cc_share_3km)` share), with **`r sprintf("%.0f%%", s$core_share_of_new)`** (+`r comma(round(s$cc_new_core))`) on tightly aligned core links (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", s$cc_share_core)` share).
2. **Nodal clustering vs rural gaps:** Commute demand clusters around **Aylesbury**, **Banbury**, **Uxbridge/Denham**, and **Amersham**; rural mid-corridor sections (Calvert–Finmere) depend heavily on **leisure/tourism** and **e-bikes**.
3. **E-bikes shift the distance curve:** Unpowered cycling peaks at `2–6 km`, whereas **e-bikes** unlock the **`6–15 km` inter-settlement band**.

```{r fig-dist-lad}
#| fig-cap: "2011 commute cycling uptake in the 3 km catchment: (A) new cyclists by distance band (Corridor Central vs additional e-bike uplift); (B) baseline vs Corridor Central cyclists by origin Local Authority District."
#| fig-width: 10.2
#| fig-height: 4.0
#| dpi: 300
plot_dist_lad(dat)
```

## Worked Example, Leisure Extension & Temporal Lag {#sec-worked-example}

### King's Sutton to Banbury (`E01027288 -> E01028435`)

- **Observed 2011 baseline:** $N_{ij} = `r s$ex_n`$ commuters (`r s$ex_cyc` cyclists, `r s$ex_walk` walker, **`r s$ex_car_drv` car drivers** [`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * s$ex_car_drv / s$ex_n)`%], `r s$ex_car_pax` car passengers, `r s$ex_bus` bus, `r s$ex_rail` rail); $d_{ij} = `r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_dist)`\text{ km}$, slope $g_{ij} = `r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_slope)`\%$. Centroids sit `r round(s$ex_o_dist)` m and `r round(s$ex_d_dist)` m from the spine with $\phi_{ij} = `r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_phi)`$, giving $\omega_{ij} = `r sprintf("%.4f", s$ex_omega)`$.
- **PCT propensities & corridor uptake:** Evaluating @eq-corridor-uptake between observed baseline (`0`), *Go Dutch* ($p^{\text{Dutch}} = `r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_p_dutch)`\%$, `r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_dutch)` cyclists), and *E-bikes* ($p^{\text{ebike}} = `r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_p_ebike)`\%$, `r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_ebike)` cyclists) yields **`r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_cc)` steady-state commute cyclists** (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", s$ex_cc_share)` share) under **Corridor Central** (`r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_trips_day)` one-way trips/day at AMAT's `1.9` return factor, **`r comma(round(s$ex_km_yr))` cycle-km/yr** over `220` days) and **`r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_ch)` cyclists** (`r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_ch_trips_day)` trips/day) under **Corridor High (E-bikes)**.
- **Car diversion sensitivity:** Proportional non-cycle diversion implies **`r sprintf("%.1f%%", s$ex_car_div_pct)`** (`r sprintf("%.2f", s$ex_car_div_cyc)` cyclists) divert from car driver — more than double AMAT's `24%` national urban default (`+6%` taxi; @dft2025amat).

Further diagnostic plots for this pair and three Buckinghamshire/Uxbridge comparisons appear in [Methods & Appendix](methods.qmd#sec-more-examples).

### Extending to Leisure & Exercise/Pleasure Trips

As documented in [Methods & Appendix](methods.qmd#sec-purpose), commuting accounts for only **{{< var nts_cycle_commute_pct >}}** of cycling trips (NTS) and **{{< var als_cycle_travel_time_pct >}}** of cycling time (ALS), whereas leisure represents **{{< var nts_cycle_leisure_pct >}}** of trips and **{{< var als_cycle_leisure_time_pct >}}** of minutes. Following @nellthorp2026 (§1.4.1, Table 2), appraisal must separate **Exercise & Pleasure** (marginal $VTT = 0$, full Journey Ambience & health benefits, lower car-diversion MECs) from **Other Non-Work Utility** (shopping, education, station access). We propose a two-tier extension:

- **Tier 1 (Screening):** Apply calibrated purpose multipliers (`1.5×` local leisure + `0.5×` other utility on `King's Sutton–Banbury` adds `+13.5` leisure and `+4.5` other-utility trips/day to `8.97` commute trips).
- **Tier 2 (Full corridor):** Run a spatial gravity model linking LSOAs, rail stations, and OSM campsites to greenway attractors with longer leisure decay ($L \approx 6\text{–}9\text{ km}$) calibrated to rural trail counters.

### Behavioural Ramp-Up Convolved with AMAT Health Lags

Over ATE's **40-year appraisal period** (3.5% transport / 1.5% health discounting; @nellthorp2026 §2.3; @hmt2026greenbook), AMAT applies 100% demand in Year 1 plus a 5-year linear physiological health lag. Because real-world route uptake builds over 3–8 years [@goodman2014], we convolve a **Bass diffusion S-curve** [@bass1969] with AMAT's 5-year health lag (equations in [Methods & Appendix](methods.qmd#sec-temporal-equations)).

```{r fig-lag}
#| fig-cap: "40-year trajectory (2030–2069) on King's Sutton–Banbury (Corridor Central): (A) annual commute trips under instant jump vs 3-, 5-, and 8-yr Bass ramp-up; (B) effective health-benefit share after convolving behavioural adoption with AMAT's 5-yr health lag."
#| fig-width: 10.2
#| fig-height: 4.0
#| dpi: 300
plot_lag_profiles(dat)
```

```{r tbl-lag-pv}
tbl_lag_pv(dat)
```

Under the **5-year Central ramp-up**, 40-year transport PV falls by **`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (1 - s$pv_t_central))`**, whereas health PV falls by **`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (1 - s$pv_h_central))`** because `1.5%` health discounting weights later decades more heavily than `3.5%` transport discounting.

## Illustrative Economic Scale & Double-Counting Guardrails {#sec-appraisal}

Passing just the **core aligned commute subset** (`r comma(s$n_pairs_core)` pairs, +`r comma(round(s$cc_new_core))` cyclists = +`r comma(round(s$core_new_trips_day))` daily trips, mean distance **`r sprintf("%.2f", s$mean_dist_core_new)` km**, `prop_on_scheme = 0.72`, `220` days/yr, `2030–2069`, `24%` AMAT default car diversion) through [`railactive/amat`](https://github.com/railactive/amat) yields **£`r sprintf("%.1f", s$amat_tot_inst)`m** PVB instant jump, or **£`r sprintf("%.1f", s$amat_tot_lag)`m** (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", -s$amat_lag_drop_pct)`) with the 5-year ramp-up — before adding TATE3030 morbidity, walking, education, or leisure/tourism.

```{r tbl-amat-scale}
#| tbl-colwidths: [26, 13, 13, 12, 36]
tbl_amat_scale(dat)
```

Because **`r sprintf("%.0f%%", s$health_amb_pct)`** of core commute PVB sits in Health and Journey Ambience, all outputs will enforce @nellthorp2026 (Table 13) double-counting rules via the 4-table hand-off schema in [Methods & Appendix](methods.qmd#sec-outputs):

::: {.callout-important}
### Double-Counting Compliance Summary (Nellthorp et al. 2026, Table 13)

1. **User benefits vs health (Recs 1–2):** Retain $\theta \approx 0$ so Journey Ambience and AMAT/TATE3030 health benefits remain additive.
2. **Rule of a Half (§2.4):** Apply RoH *only* to $\Delta CS$ / Journey Ambience — never halve physical-activity health benefits or MECs.
3. **User benefits vs safety (Recs 3–6):** Journey Ambience ({{< var ambience_offroad_rate >}}) embeds users' perceived safety WTP; add only *external* casualty outcomes and mode-shift safety MECs.
4. **Place quality (Recs 7–10):** Value origin/destination place quality only for dwell/movements strictly outside modelled trips.
5. **Exercise & Pleasure VTT (§1.4.1):** Set marginal $VTT = 0$ for Exercise & Pleasure trips while retaining Journey Ambience and health benefits.
:::
